lines.caption: A parcel arrives for Maya. She paid for a navy sweater, size medium.
Is this it? She can't see the colour. The size tag is a bump under her fingers.
Until now, knowing meant waiting for someone else to look.
Today her phone checks it, and tells her. On her own.
Buying online got easier. What comes after the parcel did not.
One in two disabled shoppers who needed a return had problems doing it.
This is Sightline. Shop by voice, and pay only for what you actually got.
Maya is a persona. This panel shows what her screen reader says.
Before money moves, a template, not the model, reads back exactly what she'll pay.
She says, yeah, probably fine. That isn't a yes, so nothing is paid.
Okay, I'll wait. Nothing is paid. Say 'confirm purchase' when you're ready.
Confirm purchase. Claude Haiku checks her words again, on its own.
PayPal authorizes $36.72 and holds it until the check.
Claude Opus reads the size tag. A second reader must agree before it's sure.
This probably isn't what you ordered, but I'm not completely sure.
Size L, not M. Charcoal, not navy. It won't guess: it says how sure it is.
She says it's wrong. Her agent signs an evidence pack, and reads her a summary first.
The store's own agent checks the signature, and offers a replacement inside the store's policy.
Maya wants her money back, so she declines. The revised offer: release the hold.
PayPal voids the authorization, and the hold is released.
Nothing was captured. The money never left her account.
Underneath: a template readback, two keys, and an eight-guard payment gate.
Model text alone can never move money.
PayPal authorizes, captures or voids. Every step is signed.
1 false alarm on 210 matching items. Image matching with CLIP: 189.
Zero payment breaches in 60 trick listings, from PayPal's own sandbox records. A simulated naive agent: 50.
And it's weak on colour: it caught 0 of 53 colour mismatches. On most of the rest, it says not sure.
Pay after the check. Not sure, instead of a guess. Money back from the store's own agent.
Maya checked her own parcel, and knew. Sightline is built for blind and low-vision shoppers.
